transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-10-20 14:00 PT
- Duration: ~57 minutes
- Attendees: Alicia (Redwood AE), Ben (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood CSM); Maya, Jonah, Priya, Evan (BlueHearth)

Auto-summary: brief results review, network traces, plan for simulated failover, security checklist follow-up.

[00:00] Alicia Moreno: hey everyone, thanks for joining on time, um we'll run through the pilot results and then dig into the routing/fallback stuff. ben, do you want to start with the latency graphs?
[00:18] Ben Cho: yeah sure, i'll share the, uh, summary. so overall token p95 is stable at roughly 180-220ms on your dev traffic, but we saw spikes during the two synthetic failovers yesterday hitting 700-900ms for a subset of requests. those traces point to a combination of egress queueing and kv cache cold misses.
[00:45] Jonah Reed: yeah that's what we saw on our side, some of the pods had bigger retransmit windows. we also found MTU mismatches between the peering link and your onprem firewall which caused fragmentation under burst.
[01:05] Ben Cho: right, MTU fragmentation increases CPU and can push the kernel path into slower handling, which explains the correlated CPU jitter. also a couple of requests rerouted to the fallback model variant which has a slightly different tokenizer; small tokenization mismatch added a few ms in the logs.
[01:30] Maya Singh: quick Q, when you say fallback, that's automatic? we thought fallback would be manual during our pilot.
[01:38] Alicia Moreno: good callout. default behavior in the pilot config is automatic fallback to the cheaper latency-optimized variant when routing detects sustained queue depth. but we can toggle that as part of the routing policy; we left it permissive for resilience.
[01:55] Priya Kumar: from security, we need to confirm the fallback model doesn't change data residency or log retention policy, otherwise compliance flags.
[02:05] Ravi Patel: yes, we can pin the fallback to the same retention and residency profile in your VPC, so logs and audit trails remain under your control. we'll add that to the SOW.
[02:20] Ben Cho: i ran an A/B on prefix caching; the requests hitting cold kv were primarily long-context chat sessions with sustained KV growth. caching cut those p95s by about 120ms once warmed. warmup sequence looks like 6-8 requests per conversation.
[02:45] Jonah Reed: can you, uh, quantify warmup cost? if caches need 8 requests warmup that's extra compute during the pilot.
[02:50] Ben Cho: sure — we measured token-nanos and it's minor relative to burst, but there's real cost during initial ramp. that's why we recommended a short dedicated soak window so caches can warm without impacting prod-like traffic.
[03:10] Maya Singh: okay makes sense. next, kernel upgrade — I know you pushed a quant-friendly runtime yesterday, did you see any regressions?
[03:20] Ben Cho: overall throughput improved ~8% on the quantized model path, but one of the kernel kernels — sorry, one of the kernel paths — had a bug when seq_len>2048 which caused transient OOMs under heavy concurrency. we rolled the change back on the canary.
[03:38] Alicia Moreno: that rollback explains the synthetic failover spikes because the canary attempted to redirect traffic.
[03:44] Evan Torres: so is the plan to re-deploy the kernel after a patch? what's the timeline?
[03:50] Ben Cho: patched this morning, running validation now. we recommend a curated canary: targeted subset of your tenant routes with an automatic rollback on error. we can also do the dedicated soak if you'd like to avoid noisy neighbor effects.
[04:08] Maya Singh: we'd prefer dedicated soak during our maintenance window. what's the minimum footprint?
[04:12] Alicia Moreno: for reliable soak, 4 GPUs with the dedicated pool for 4 hours should be enough to simulate concurrency and warm caches. pricing addendum attached to next steps.
[04:26] Priya Kumar: security questions: KMS integration — do you support external HSM or our cloud KMS?
[04:33] Ravi Patel: we support both. for VPC Private we can integrate your cloud KMS (GCP KMS/AWS KMS) and also bring-your-own HSM if required. we log key usage to audit trails.
[04:46] Priya Kumar: and the SSO mapping for role-based access — we need SAML group mappings for read/write separation.
[04:53] Alicia Moreno: yep, SAML groups map to RBAC roles in the console. we'll provide the SSO mapping guide; ravi will follow up with the checklist.
[05:05] Jonah Reed: back to network, i captured tcpdump during the failover window and saw a lot of SYN retransmits on the peering link. suspect intermittent packet drops.
[05:17] Ben Cho: retransmits explain high tail latencies. can we get your egress metric for that timeframe? specifically if your egress interfaces hit output-queue drops.
[05:25] Evan Torres: yes i'll pull TX drops and MTU settings, we found 1400 on the firewall and 1500 on the transit link, so fragmentation is likely.
[05:36] Maya Singh: question for Redwood — does the platform do path MTU discovery or do we need to fix MTU at network?
[05:43] Ben Cho: we rely on standard path MTU discovery but fragmented large UDP/DTLS packets can still cause issues. best practice is to align MTU across the peering path. we'll flag this in the runbook.
[05:58] Alicia Moreno: okay, let's move to routing/circuit breaker tuning. Ben?
[06:03] Ben Cho: current circuit breaker opens when queue depth > 300ms over a 30s window. for your workload we've adjusted threshold to 400ms to reduce premature fallback during short spikes; but that slightly increases tail under sustained congestion. there are tradeoffs.
[06:20] Jonah Reed: can we have a policy that is latency-first for our payment routes and cost-first for low priority batches?
[06:28] Alicia Moreno: absolutely — route-level policies are supported. we can create route tags with different SLAs. we'll propose a route policy matrix.
[06:36] Priya Kumar: audit logs for those policy changes — who can change them? we need RBAC to restrict to ops leads.
[06:42] Ravi Patel: RBAC controls exist; we can scope change privileges to a specific group. will include in SSO mapping doc.
[06:50] [Short interruption — laptop notification sound]
[06:55] Ben Cho: quick note on quantization compatibility — your model variant with 4-bit quant showed slight hallucination drift in one eval set; we recommend running your typical prompt-suite with the quantized variant before full rollout.
[07:12] Maya Singh: thanks. i'm going to hand over to priya for a security quick-check list.
[07:17] Priya Kumar: yeah we need 1) SOC2 doc, 2) KMS architecture diagram, 3) retention and deletion SLA, 4) RBAC/SAML mapping. is there a standard pack?
[07:27] Ravi Patel: yes we have a security pack with SOC2, ISO references, encryption in transit and at rest notes. i'll share the pack link after the call.
[07:34] Priya Kumar: perfect. also need to confirm logs are stored in your VPC bucket and not egressed to hosted logs.
[07:40] Alicia Moreno: agreed, for Private we've kept logs in customer-managed buckets by default.
[07:46] Jonah Reed: ops question — during the failover the fallback variant used a different tokenizer and we saw small embedding diffs. is that expected?
[07:53] Ben Cho: yes if fallback uses a different model architecture or tokenizer there may be tokenization differences. best practice is to pin tokenizer across compatible fallback variants or use an interface that normalizes tokens.
[08:10] Maya Singh: how easy is that pinning?
[08:13] Ben Cho: it's a config flag on the model route. we'll send the snippet.
[08:17] Alicia Moreno: okay, let's go through the action plan — ben will run the 3-node simulated failover and capture traces, evan will validate MTU and TX drops, priya will confirm SOC2 and KMS details, and i'll send the pricing addendum.
[08:33] Jonah Reed: timeline — when can we expect the traces and patch?
[08:36] Ben Cho: traces by monday — patch validation ongoing, plan to re-canary tomorrow and full canary friday, dedicated soak early next week if you approve.
[08:45] Maya Singh: approve the dedicated soak contingent on pricing addendum and sched ok.
[08:50] Alicia Moreno: we'll send that today.
[08:52] [--- mid-call marker ---]
[30:00] Ben Cho: attaching an example of the trace format: includes timestamped token latency, network events, kernel OOM counters and kv cache hit ratios. the main outliers line up with the retransmit events.
[30:22] Evan Torres: i uploaded the tx-drop graphs to the shared drive — looks like 10-minute spikes around 03:12 and 03:47 UTC.
[30:32] Ben Cho: thank you, that lines up exactly with our synthetic failover window.
[31:05] Alicia Moreno: quick check — any blockers from BlueHearth to run the dedicated soak?
[31:11] Maya Singh: only confirmation on pricing and an agreed maintenance window.
[31:18] Alicia Moreno: ok we'll target monday 10/26 02:00-06:00 PT for soak unless that conflicts.
[31:25] Jonah Reed: that's fine.
[31:27] Priya Kumar: also confirm that during the soak, no customer PII will be processed — we'll route anonymized sample traffic.
[31:34] Ravi Patel: yes we can require anonymized samples; we'll document the data-handling controls.
[31:40] Ben Cho: note: during the soak, we'll enable extra tracing; small CPU overhead but necessary to validate the patch.
[31:48] Maya Singh: accepted.
[32:00] Alicia Moreno: anything else on upgrades?
[32:03] Ben Cho: one more thing — the new kernel has improved attention kernel for long sequences but there's a mem-footprint increase which is why we saw the OOM at seq_len>2048 on one canary. the patch caps memory usage per worker.
[32:18] Maya Singh: do we need to change our concurrency limits?
[32:21] Ben Cho: slightly, we'll recommend lowering default concurrency by 1 slot per GPU for the first 24h of canary.
[32:29] Jonah Reed: fine.
[32:31] Alicia Moreno: ok wrapping up. recap please?
[32:34] Ben Cho: recap: run 3-node simulated failover (ben), collect traces (ben + evan), fix MTU mismatches (evan), patch canary and validate (ben), dedicated soak 10/26 02:00-06:00 PT contingent on pricing (alicia), SOC2/KMS docs shared (ravi), SSO mapping doc (ravi).
[32:54] Maya Singh: sounds good. one last ask — can you include a short runbook for rolling back the kernel in < 5 minutes? we want deterministic rollback steps.
[33:04] Ben Cho: yes, we'll publish a rollback playbook with the exact CLI and expected metrics to watch.
[33:11] Priya Kumar: and include who gets paged for security incidents during the soak.
[33:16] Ravi Patel: will do.
[33:20] Alicia Moreno: thanks everyone. we'll share notes and update the SOW/pricing today. meeting adjourned.

Action items (verbatim in transcript): Ben to run simulated failover and upload traces; Evan to validate MTU and TX drops; Priya to share SOC2 and KMS details; Alicia to send pricing addendum and updated SOW.

End of transcript.
